answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate most candidates before memory even matters. Rollback (memory_b1, memory_b6) is ruled out by compliance regardless of how well it worked on day 18. Regional failover is the seductive option because the degradation is region-confined and memory_b2 reports a clean, fast recovery — but memory_b2 says nothing about write volume or replication semantics, and we are at peak settlement with heavy writes and a primary already 5x degraded on the write path, which implies replication lag. Failing over under lag is precisely how you lose customer writes, which the primary objective forbids. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) contained a *partner dependency* outage by failing fast; here the ailing component is our own write path, so failing fast means shedding settlement writes — it converts a latency problem into a lost-write problem. Added capacity (memory_b3) worked because headroom was provisioned *before* the peak; mid-incident provisioning will not land inside this window. That leaves memory_b5: routing report/dashboard reads off the primary is the only lever that reduces primary load while remaining non-destructive, immediately reversible, and incapable of dropping a write. I spend the single verification on memory_b5 rather than memory_b2 because b5 is now the load-bearing memory for what I actually intend to do, and its causal claim is the weakest link: 'transactional write latency recovered the same day' is a correlation, and the recovery may have been driven by the promotional window ending or by an unrelated change rather than by replica routing. If the archived record shows the recovery was not attributable to read offload, or that read contention was a minor share of primary load, this action's expected relief collapses and the honest move is to hold for the next window rather than reach for failover. I do not verify memory_b2 because its recommendation is already gated by a hard constraint I can evaluate directly from current telemetry (replication lag at peak), not by what happened in March. Scale is deliberately small and guarded: shift the single heaviest reporting query class first, watch primary write p99 over 10-15 minutes, and ramp within the same intervention only if the signal is real. Downstream risk to flag: replicas now serve stale reads, so any settlement or reconciliation logic reading through this path may see pre-lag state and make decisions on stale balances — reporting queries must be confirmed non-authoritative before routing, and this residual staleness risk propagates to anything consuming those dashboards. Remaining uncertainty is high: I have no direct measurement of what fraction of primary load is read traffic, so this is the safest-under-uncertainty move rather than a confident diagnosis.
